input.quote: (a) Ono shall have the right (but not the obligation) to Manufacture and/or package, or engage a Subcontractor to Manufacture, Ono's requirements of particular Materials (e.g., Ono's requirements of Drug Substance or Ono's requirements of Drug Product of a particular Product) related to any Product for the Ono Territory.
input.rationale: No sourcing exclusivity is imposed on us. Article IX expressly makes Array's supply optional for us: Section 9.4(a) gives Ono "the right (but not the obligation)" to manufacture or engage a Subcontractor for its requirements of Materials (with a supporting Array Know-How technology transfer), and Section 9.4(b) provides only that "Ono shall have the right to obtain from Array Ono's commercial requirements" — no all-requirements or sole-supplier covenant, and Section 2.1(b) grants Ono a worldwide manufacturing licence extendable to Third Party manufacturers. This meets the preferred position (no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on the Customer). Noted but not flagged: Section 8.2 (Exclusivity of Efforts) restricts us from Commercializing a Competing Product in the Ono Territory for a redacted period, but that is a mutual field non-compete (binding Array and its Controlled Affiliates equally, with royalty-term termination if Array competes) rather than a restriction on our freedom to source Materials, so it falls outside this sourcing rule and its symmetry benefits us.
